name: Bianca Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, on the junior calls and chats rota, and still learning the billing system. I finished secondary school. My pay is about usual for this job, but I take longer than the stronger agents to sort a disputed payment. I do not use AI tools; I want to see the account record and ask someone when I am unsure.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Jules, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. We have about four months of expenses saved. There are some other centres nearby, but moving jobs would still mean changing our childcare routine. I like helping a customer understand a bill; the timer on my screen makes me rush.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau should leave enough time for an agent to read a bill before answering. I do not want a small shortcut to become a new speed target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job and pay are mostly safe in this picture. Four months saved covers a surprise better than none, but the mortgage and school costs still sit on the table.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking billing calls and ask a colleague to show me the account check when I get stuck. In the first year of small change, I’d put a little from each pay into the reserve and ask the staff group to track whether the new timer reduces paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, though I am not frightened of losing the job right now. I know a small change can still become a harder target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the staff group measure?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the staff group to collect our actual paid hours for a month, with names left off the list. If the hours stay the same, I can stop worrying about that part.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which household costs stay on your mind?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Jules (my partner) and I use a paper list for mortgage, food and school shoes. A new shortcut at work does not remove our mortgage, food and school-shoe bills.

say: I’d ask for **time to read bills** before answering.
I’d oppose a new **speed target** built on small shortcuts.
think: I think my **job and pay** are mostly safe.
I still watch our **mortgage and school costs**.
I want to know whether **paid hours** stay level after the new shortcut.
do: Keep **taking billing calls** and asking for account checks in 2026.
Save each pay and help the **staff group** track paid hours in the first year.
S0.quote: A new shortcut at work does not remove our mortgage, food and school-shoe bills.
fieldNote: Her **four-month cushion** softens, but does not erase, mortgage pressure.
She wants a **group hour count** before concluding the shortcut is harmless.
Her **paper bill list** grounds her worry in ordinary costs.

steps.text: Keep answering billing calls and check uncertain accounts with a colleague
Add a little from each pay to the four-month reserve
Help the staff group collect one month of anonymised paid hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will take routine billing answers first, so the staff group should ask what happens to our paid hours. I would want customers to reach a person when the software gives a wrong amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could lose hours because routine calls are the part I do most confidently. I am still slow on difficult bills, and another centre might be using the same software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d help the staff group write a request for monthly error and hour figures. In the first year routine answers move, I’d apply for a posted billing role at another centre only if the written hours cover our mortgage, and take paid difficult-case practice here if offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Four months of expenses saved gives me time for a job search, but not time to wait forever for a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would go in the group letter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the number of wrong bill amounts and the hours actually paid to agents each month. The staff group could take that request as one letter rather than five private grumbles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you learn harder bills?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would sit with a skilled agent on a paid shift and work through three disputed bills. I would not buy a course without a posted job and a wage attached to it.

say: I’d ask the **staff group** to demand error and hour figures.
I’d defend a **human appeal** for wrong bills.
think: I think **routine billing hours** could shrink for me.
I doubt a nearby centre is **automatically safer**.
I need **written hours** before changing jobs for our mortgage.
do: Help draft a **group letter** on paid hours and errors in 2026.
Seek **mortgage-covering billing work** and take paid difficult-case practice if offered.
S1.quote: Four months of expenses saved gives me time for a job search, but not time to wait forever for a promise.
fieldNote: Her **routine calls** expose her junior role to early change.
The **group letter** asks for concrete error and hour figures.
She accepts **paid practice** but rejects an unposted course.

steps.text: Help staff group request monthly wrong-bill and paid-hour figures
Apply for posted billing work only with written mortgage-covering hours if routine calls move
Practise three disputed bills beside an agent on paid time if offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 could take almost all of our billing calls and checks. I would ask the staff group to seek written notice, paid retraining for posted jobs and a customer appeal route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job could end in 2028 even though robots come around 2031. A headset needs thinking work, not a robot hand; four months saved would go fast with a mortgage and two children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d join the staff group in putting those demands in writing and pause a planned kitchen repair that can safely wait. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception job with hours covering the mortgage and take a funded course only if required for that vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. The mortgage letter arrives whether the company has finished its staffing plan or not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which repair could wait?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Jules (my partner) the kitchen cabinet can wait if it is safe to use. We would keep that money in the account for the mortgage and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would carry the demands?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the staff group to take one clear proposal to management and share the answer with everyone. A private chat with my supervisor would not tell the whole floor what rights they have.

say: I’d ask for **written notice** and a customer appeal route.
I’d press the **staff group** for paid training tied to posted jobs.
think: I think my **job could end** when AGI arrives in 2028.
I know **four months saved** is short against a mortgage.
do: Join a **group proposal** and delay a safe kitchen repair in 2026.
Apply for **posted reception work** after 2028; take only vacancy-required funded training.
feel: **Alarmed** by the job and mortgage risk.
S2.quote: The mortgage letter arrives whether the company has finished its staffing plan or not.
fieldNote: She anchors risk at **2028 thinking AI**, not the robot date.
Her **staff group** carries a written proposal to management.
The **repair delay** is conditional on the kitchen remaining safe.

steps.text: Join the staff group’s written request for notice, paid job training and appeals
Delay the kitchen cabinet repair only while it remains safe to use
Apply for posted paid reception work with mortgage-covering hours after 2028
Take funded training only if required for the posted paid reception vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives workers a few years to bargain for the rules before the software takes calls. I would ask our staff group to press for paid time on difficult bills and a list of real vacancies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn the hard billing cases over five years if the centre gives me paid practice. I still expect fewer agents when full AGI can reason through the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d help the staff group ask for one paid practice shift each month and take it if the centre agrees. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for a posted billing or reception job with written mortgage-covering hours, and move only if Jules and I can keep the children’s school route workable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years gives me time to test real work. I do not want another course poster; I want to see a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which cases would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would work through a wrong fee, a missing payment and a disputed refund on the paid rota. I would keep my notes so another employer can see what I learned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for a job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Jules (my partner) and I would check the travel time to school before moving for work. A higher wage is no help if nobody can get the children there.

say: I’d ask the **staff group** for paid billing practice.
I’d demand a **real vacancy list** before people take courses.
think: I think I could learn **hard billing cases** on paid shifts.
I still expect **fewer agents** after full AGI.
do: Seek and take **monthly paid practice** through the group if offered from 2026.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2031 with mortgage-covering hours.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to test real work.
S3.quote: I do not want another course poster; I want to see a paid shift.
fieldNote: She links **paid practice** to three specific billing problems.
A move must preserve the **children’s school route**.
She wants the **group** to secure terms, not one private promise.

steps.text: Help staff group request a paid difficult-bill shift each month
Practise three billing cases monthly on paid time if the centre agrees
Apply for posted work with written mortgage-covering hours after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to set fair rules for customer appeals and paid learning. I would ask the staff group to keep checking the agreement each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can earn and save more before 2036, though my phone work may still go when thinking AI arrives. The robots come around 2039, which is later than my desk risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d stay on calls, put a fixed part of each pay into savings and help the staff group ask for yearly staffing figures. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted staffed billing role only with written hours that cover our mortgage and a school route Jules and I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, not carefree. A decade is long enough to build a cushion, but the mortgage still comes each month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which staffing number matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for paid hours, not just the number of calls answered. A report that leaves wages out could make a shrinking floor look healthy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the household move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Jules (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a workable trip. I have seen people move too quickly for a job that did not last.

say: I’d ask the **staff group** to request yearly figures on paid agent hours.
I’d defend **customer appeals** and paid learning.
think: I think I could **save more** before 2036.
I know **thinking AI** may still take my phone work.
do: Keep **calling**, save from each pay and seek group reports from 2026.
Apply for **staffed billing work** after 2036 only with written mortgage-covering hours and a manageable school route.
feel: **Uneasy** about later change and current bills.
S4.quote: A report that leaves wages out could make a shrinking floor look healthy.
fieldNote: She wants **paid hours** in reports, not only completed calls.
Her **moderate reserve** supports saving over a decade.
A **signed offer** and school route condition any move.

steps.text: Keep answering billing calls while the centre staffs them
Put a fixed part of each pay into household savings
Help staff group request yearly figures on paid agent hours
Apply to posted staffed billing jobs after 2036 with written mortgage-covering hours and workable school route

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Cheap thinking AI could take the calls before I am fluent in the hard cases, and four months of savings would run down with a mortgage. Staff should bargain together for written notice, paid time to learn a posted role and a way for customers to appeal wrong bills.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who carries the mistake when a bill is wrong. A customer cannot argue with a silent screen, and an agent cannot fix an answer without seeing how it was made.

headlineQuote: A customer cannot argue with a silent screen, and an agent cannot fix an answer without seeing how it was made.
portrait: At **43**, Bianca is a junior billing agent after secondary school and earns typical pay.
She and Jules support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with four months of expenses saved.
She avoids **AI tools** and wants to inspect accounts herself before answering.
She uses a **staff group** to seek notice, paid practice and customer appeal rights.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her calls before she masters hard billing work.
whatWouldHelp: A **group agreement** on notice, paid training for a posted role and customer appeal rights would help.
